subject: Future Tech
title: What Is Quantum Computing?
description: Learn What Is Quantum Computing? in one minute.

hook.text: Classical computers use bits: zeros and ones. Quantum computers use qubits that can be both at once.

buildup.text: This property, superposition, lets quantum machines explore many solutions in parallel instead of one by one.

discovery.text: Richard Feynman proposed the idea in 1981. Only a quantum machine could simulate quantum physics, he argued.

twist.text: But qubits are incredibly fragile. A tiny vibration or stray photon can collapse the quantum state instantly.

climax.text: Despite that, IBM and Google now operate machines with over a thousand qubits on real hardware.

punchline.text: Quantum computing trades certainty for power.

quiz.question: Who first proposed the idea of quantum computing?
